topics.label: Introduction to the lecture on inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate recognition through PAMPs, DAMPs and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immune receptors distinguish signs of infection or damage and detect them in the appropriate cellular location.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how toll-like receptors translate microbial recognition into immune responses shaped by the location and context of detection.

topics.label: Non-TLR sensing and inflammasome-driven inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how sensing pathways beyond toll-like receptors trigger inflammation that can also contribute to inflammatory disease.

topics.label: Sentinel-cell signalling and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how activated sentinel cells generate inflammatory signals that mobilise immune cells to the site of infection.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how drainage from infected tissue enables dendritic cells to carry evidence of infection to lymph nodes for adaptive immune activation.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation produces life-threatening systemic effects.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammation subsides through a changing balance between inflammatory stimulation and inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and the persistence of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the limits of restoring damaged tissue to normal, including why persistent inflammation may require containment rather than complete elimination of its cause.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture on complement
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and identifies the subject of the next session.
